answer.sourceLine: This exact line appears in Leopold Bloom’s interior monologue near the end of the “Nausicaa” episode of Ulysses (1922) — confirmed directly against the novel’s text.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: So it returns. Think you're escaping and run into yourself. Longest way round is the shortest way home. And just when he and she. Circus horse walking in a ring.
trail: The line appears verbatim in the “Nausicaa” episode of Ulysses, in Bloom’s closing interior monologue on Sandymount Strand ↗.
Ulysses was first published complete on 2 February 1922 by Shakespeare and Company in Paris, per Wikipedia’s Ulysses article ↗.
The novel is in the U.S. public domain and freely available in full at Project Gutenberg ↗ and Standard Ebooks ↗.
source.excerptNote: Popular quotations of this line usually clip it down to just the two sentences given, dropping the surrounding fragments of Bloom's stream of consciousness.
source.rightsNote: Ulysses was first published in 1922 and has been in the U.S. public domain since 2019 under the 95-year rule; the full text is freely available from multiple archives.

author.heading: James Joyce
author.bio: James Joyce was an Irish modernist writer best known for Dubliners, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, and his 1922 novel Ulysses, widely regarded as one of the most important works of 20th-century literature. He spent most of his adult life in continental Europe, writing obsessively about the Dublin he had left behind.

context.heading: Where it comes from
lead: This meditation on cyclical return comes from the final stretch of the “Nausicaa” episode, as Leopold Bloom sits alone on Sandymount Strand after Gerty MacDowell has gone, his mind drifting through memories of Molly, old friends at Dolphin’s Barn, and the sense that life’s paths curve back on themselves — “returning not the same,” as the passage puts it just before.

“Nausicaa” is also the episode that made Ulysses notorious: its serialization in The Little Review triggered a 1921 U.S. obscenity prosecution that kept the complete novel banned in America until a 1933 court ruling cleared it for publication.
